2608.14058.title: Voxel-based 3D Facies Segmentation from Seismic Data: A Comparative Study
2608.14058.paper_summary: Seismic facies segmentation has emerged as a significant challenge in geophysics, requiring robust methods and systems to effectively identify geologically analogous facies with limited labeled data. Although existing studies have shown promising results in 2D facies segmentation, they often preprocess the original 3D seismic volumes into sets of 2D slices, typically the inline and crossline directions, and treat this problem as a purely 2D segmentation task. This simplification introduces discontinuities across slices and fails to preserve the spatial and structural continuity in 3D seismic data, thus limiting the model's ability to learn coherent geological patterns. In this work, we present a comparative and reproducible benchmark for voxel-based 3D seismic facies segmentation, built upon publicly available seismic volumes including the Netherlands F3 and the Parihaka datasets, with standardized data splits and evaluation metrics. By evaluating the three representative families of modern 3D segmentation architectures, we establish strong baseline results that highlight the potential and remaining challenges for future research in this domain.
2608.14058.paper_summary_zh: 地震相分割已成為地球物理學中的一項重大挑戰，需要穩健的方法和系統來有效識別具有有限標記數據的地質類似相。儘管現有研究在2D相分割中顯示出有希望的結果，但它們通常將原始的3D地震體積預處理為一組2D切片，通常是內線和交叉線方向，並將此問題視為純粹的2D分割任務。這種簡化引入了切片之間的不連續性，無法保持3D地震數據中的空間和結構連續性，從而限制了模型學習一致地質模式的能力。在這項工作中，我們提出了一個基於體素的3D地震相分割的比較和可重複基準，基於公開可用的地震體積，包括荷蘭F3和Parihaka數據集，並具有標準化的數據劃分和評估指標。通過評估三種代表性的現代3D分割架構，我們建立了強有力的基準結果，突顯了該領域未來研究的潛力和剩餘挑戰。
